lines.text: A civil war burns between the stars.
For a generation, the Empire has answered every question with a fleet, and every objection with silence.
Now a handful of rebels have stolen something it cannot afford to lose. The design of a station large enough to end a world.
One ship carries that secret, and it is running out of dark to hide in.
Above the desert world of Tatooine, a stolen secret races through the dark.
Below, twin suns burn over an ocean of sand. A world so poor, so far from anything that matters, that nobody thinks to look here.
That is precisely why they came.
For eleven more seconds, the sky is empty.
She is a diplomatic corvette. Unarmoured, barely armed, built to carry envoys, not fugitives.
Inside her is a princess of the Alliance, and the plans she was sent to deliver.
She very nearly made it.
The thing behind her is a mile and a half of grey armour, and it is in no hurry at all.
It does not need to be quick. It only needs to be inevitable.
Her deflectors hold for ninety seconds.
Then the turbolasers find her drives, and the small ship goes dark.
There is no distress call. There is nobody close enough to answer one.
Powerless, she is drawn in. Held in a beam she cannot break, against a hull that could swallow her whole.
Magnetic clamps take hold. Somewhere forward, a cutting charge begins to burn through a sealed door.
The crew have perhaps two minutes. They know exactly what they intend to spend them on.
Ship security. Six of them. Flak vests, and carbines meant for pirates.
They take the corridor anyway.
Hold this passage. Whatever comes through that door, hold it.
The door does not open. It comes apart.
White armour, moving in pairs, advancing behind its own fire. This is not a boarding action. It is a procedure.
It is finished in under a minute.
And then the shooting stops, which is worse.
He does not hurry either. He has never had to.
While they tear apart the forward decks, she is already moving aft.
In her hand is the complete readout of the station. Every corridor, every conduit, and one flaw its builders never found.
Every deck. Every shaft. Get this to the surface.
She has seconds, and exactly one courier the Empire will never think to search.
She gives it to a droid, and tells it where to run.
Two droids. One sealed lifeboat. No weapons, no escort, and no plan beyond the surface below.
One of them is terrified. The other has simply decided.
Into that? We shall be smashed to atoms.
The clamps release.
To the gunners above it reads as debris. No life signs. Not worth a shot.
And so the most dangerous secret of the war falls toward a desert, inside an unarmed droid that was given one instruction and no doubts at all.
Everything that comes after begins here.
